sources: Italian FM Antonio Tajani (interview), German FM Johann Wadephul (remarks), Istanbul E3+R4 meeting
fault_line: Eight countries say 'nobody approves' a new attack -- but none of them commands the US fleet. Is diplomacy restraining Trump, or just commenting on him?

sections.what_happened: Italian FM Tajani, in an interview after the Istanbul meeting, said there were signs the conflict in the Gulf could resume after the US midterm elections, and called transit fees or other restrictions on shipping through the Strait of Hormuz unacceptable. German FM Wadephul: the eight countries 'speak here with one voice when we say: enough is enough' and would use all diplomatic channels. French FM Barrot (recrawled): a new escalation 'would create nothing but losers' with serious consequences for hydrocarbon prices; the group agreed to meet at regular intervals.
sections.what_verified: Quotes carried consistently by 4+ independent regional outlets (The News PK, FMT, Aalimi Nation, SL Guardian) plus a CGTN mention; no wire seen in-window. Direct on-record quotes from named ministers at a documented meeting (group photo published by PID) -- PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM material carried by undeclared-tier outlets. Undeclared tiers do not count toward the family corroboration gate.
sections.what_disputed: Barrack ('absolutely' possible this weekend) and Trump ('may do another little Epic Fury') contradict the eight ministers' unified restraint line. The ministers control no military assets -- the restraint call is diplomatic, not operational.
sections.why_matters: While Washington floats weekend strikes, the entire region plus Europe met in Istanbul and said: nobody approves. The split between the war planners and everyone else is now on record.
sections.context: Background: UPDATE to totw-20261024-0000-07 / 0100-03 (Istanbul E3+R4) -- Tajani: 'signs the conflict could resume after the US midterm elections'; transit fees/restrictions on Hormuz shipping 'unacceptable'; Wadephul: 'enough is enough'

totw_analysis: Our read: While Washington floats weekend strikes, the entire region plus Europe met in Istanbul and said: nobody approves. The split between the war planners and everyone else is now on record. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Eight countries say 'nobody approves' a new attack -- but none of them commands the US fleet. Is diplomacy restraining Trump, or just commenting on him?
